Melissa (People Ops): Thanks for everyone who joined the security/privacy segment earlier. Quick follow-up: drop any leftover Qs about SOC2/ISO, VPCs, audit logs, KMS here and Jordan/Diego will answer. :wave:

Jordan (CISO): I'll start — short recap: we're prioritizing SOC 2 Type II (security + availability) readiness, working with an external assessor. Timeline: readiness work Q2, Type II audit ops run Q3, report target Q4 2026. ISO inquiries welcome too.

Sophie (Eng-ML): timeline makes sense — which controls specifically touch model weights and inference infra? data residency for embeddings?

Jordan (CISO): Mainly: access controls (IAM & least privilege), environment separation (hosted vs dedicated/private), encryption at rest/in transit, logging/monitoring, incident response. Model artifacts are treated as sensitive in dedicated/private; hosted API customers can opt-in for no-model-retention. Embeddings: we offer data-in-transit protection + optional customer-controlled storage for retention.

Diego (CTO): To add — Private (VPC) deployments give you a private control plane + optional on-prem package. For hosted customers we provide VPC peering and private endpoints in some regions. The runtime supports per-tenant KV isolation and no-shared-cache modes for extra isolation.

Anita (Customer Success): Customer asked today whether audit logs can be exported to their S3 or SIEM — what's current state?

Karen (Head of Product): Audit log export (S3) is in beta — retention/export UI coming next month. Default hosted retention is 90 days; enterprise plans can request 1y or custom via export. We'll have a self-serve export + push-to-Syslog/Splunk in the next quarter.

Vic (Eng-SRE): Quick perf question — does enabling KMS-backed key wrapping add request latency to inference calls?

Diego (CTO): Short answer: no meaningful per-token impact. KMS calls are used at key unwrap/wrap during deployment, signing tokens, or when rotating keys; we cache unwrapped keys in HSM session for runtime. You can expect sub-ms overhead on startup and negligible per-request overhead. :thumbsup:

Sophie (Eng-ML): How does key rotation work for customer-managed KMS?

Jordan (CISO): We support customer-managed keys (CMK) and HSM integrations. Rotation options: automatic (customer-managed schedule), manual, and annual recommended. Redwood never stores plaintext long-term for hosted — keys are wrapped. We provide rotation hooks and a rollback window. For Private, customers can keep keys entirely on-prem.

deploy-bot: deployment 1769008801 completed (private-kms-beta) :white_check_mark:

Diego (CTO): Example KMS config for Private (very small example):

```
kms_provider: aws-kms
key_alias: arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456:key/abcd-ef01
wrap_mode: envelope
rotate: true
```

Karen (Head of Product): Also noting scope for SOC2 evidence: we'll publish a controls mapping doc + redacted artifacts pack for customers in the trust center. That will include control descriptions, our procedures, and sample evidence types (logs, runbooks).

Anita (Customer Success): Can we get a one-pager for sales/CS today that summarizes retention options + KMS capabilities?

Jordan (CISO): Yes — ACTION: I'll share a SOC readiness one-pager and controls mapping by EOD Friday.

Vic (Eng-SRE): ACTION: I'll open an internal RFC for runtime key cache telemetry and a perf checklist for private KMS setups.

Melissa (People Ops): Awesome — thanks everyone. If you hit more questions drop them here. We'll pin Jordan's one-pager and the product beta signup link once available. :pin:

Jordan (CISO): FYI folks — for ISO:27001 we're scoping next quarter, but the SOC2 pipeline is our immediate focus. Happy to chat 1:1 for specific customer asks. Ping me or book time.

Sophie (Eng-ML): Thanks — can you add a note about model retention opt-in flags in the docs? I can help write.

Jordan (CISO): Please do. Sophie + Product to collaborate.

Melissa (People Ops): Closing thread soon; tagging action owners: @Jordan (SOC artifacts), @Vic (RFC/perf), @Karen (audit export beta). Thanks! :tada:
